title: The Stoic Dichotomy of Control
text:
A core tenet of Stoic philosophy is the distinction between what lies within an individual's power and what does not. This dichotomy asserts that emotional peace (ataraxia) can only be achieved by focusing effort exclusively on internal judgments, reactions, and intentions.

External events—such as natural disasters, political outcomes, or the actions of others—are deemed outside of personal control. Recognizing this boundary allows an individual to redirect energy away from fruitless concern over unchangeable variables.

The practice requires consistent rational assent, meaning one must continually evaluate whether distress stems from the event itself, or merely from the subjective judgment applied to that event.
